01 / ABOUT
Background and approach

Analytical thinking.
International experience.

I'm drawn to finance for the decisions behind the numbers: how companies assess risk, allocate capital, and plan for the long term.

At NMB Bank, I reviewed consortium lending arrangements. At Sipradi and HomePro, I worked with customer research and business systems. Together, those roles gave me a practical view of how decisions are supported by information and execution.

Living across different countries taught me to adapt quickly and work with people who see problems differently. That perspective is part of how I approach research, collaboration, and the career I'm building in finance.

Peers consistently recognized a constructive, respectful approach, while encouraging me to share my ideas more often. I see the distinction between taking initiative privately and making that initiative visible to a team.

01 Respect is a consistent professional strength.

EVIDENCEPeers rated respect for other ideas 4.0, 4.0, and 3.75/4. Comments describe a positive attitude and willingness to listen.

REASONING & ACTIONThe feedback supports a value I consider important: taking different perspectives seriously. I intend to preserve that strength while contributing my own views more decisively.

02 Preparation must translate into a stronger voice.

EVIDENCEMy SPI suggests a proactive Driver style, but 360° participation scores were 3.5, 3.0, and 3.75/4. Peers specifically encouraged me to voice ideas more often.

REASONING & ACTIONPreparation alone does not make my thinking visible. I will contribute an evidence-backed perspective earlier in discussions and communicate recommendations more directly.

03 Accountability is the next area to strengthen.

EVIDENCEQuality-of-work expectation scores rose from 92.5 to 98/100 between the first and third rounds, while accountability scores were 3, 2, and 3/4.

REASONING & ACTIONDelivering quality work is only part of effective collaboration. I will establish responsibilities and deadlines at the outset, then follow up early and constructively when work is at risk.

Next steps: contribute earlier in meetings, clarify responsibilities, and evaluate progress through follow-up feedback.
